title: Light Slovakian Pork Dumplings
description: A pungent and pillowy Slovakian dish featuring vanilla bean paste, perfect for a low-sodium diet, this recipe is made in a fondue pot and is sure to be energizing. The deglaze fond adds a rich flavor to the dish.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, vanilla bean paste, and a pinch of salt and pepper, mixing well with your hands until just combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour and egg, then add this mixture to the pork mixture, mixing until a dough forms.
Bring the low sodium chicken broth to a boil in the fondue pot, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Using a spoon, drop small balls of the dough into the simmering broth, covering the pot with a lid.
Cook the dumplings for 10 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
While the dumplings are cooking, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, then add the white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
After the dumplings have cooked, use a slotted spoon to remove them from the pot, then add the deglaze fond to the pot and stir to combine.
Serve the dumplings hot, topped with the deglaze fond and chopped parsley.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
